newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt keeps a still, wary eye on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt keeps a still, wary eye on U.S. data.

text.p: The market for Brady bonds hardly stirred on Monday with a holiday in the U.S. and concern that the sentiment which has taken prices close to record highs may be turning, traders and analysts said.
The market closes at midday and reopens on Tuesday morning.
"People are getting just a little nervous. There could an increase in U.S. rates before the (November U.S. presidential) election," one U.S. bank trader said.
The market was hurt by the U.S. Treasury fall late last week which has combined with some unsettling news out of a number of countries, notably in Latin America.
"The news coming out of the market is raising a few questionmarks," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analysts Stuart Parkinson who queried whether the market could go up any more in the short-term.
There is concern over Argentina's continued struggle to implement tough fiscal measures, while Venezuela's commitment to privatisation has come under fresh scrutiny.
A number of analysts have been fairly sanguine about last week's rebellion in Mexico, seeing it as unlikely to deflect investors from the country's surge out of recession.
But the news of last week's guerrilla attacks, combined with a weak market, has only helped to dampen sentiment, some traders said.

In his state of the nation address on Sunday, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said the country's economic crisis was over, though it would take a long time for the standard of living for ordinary Mexicans to improve.
Zedillo also fledged to fight "with the full force of the state" a new leftist guerrilla movement which erupted on the scene last week in the worst political violence in Mexico for two years.
Parkinson said it could be this week's U.S. economic data which finally hits the market. The key figure is non-farm payrolls for August, due on Friday.
About the only emerging debt to rise was Russian Vneshekonombank dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR which was bid about 1/4 of a point higher, but as with the rest of the market, trading was extremely thin.
